description: Manual-only tasks - CREATE TASK with no SCHEDULE - and the EXECUTE TASK command that runs them. A manual task shows a NULL schedule and starts SUSPENDED, where a scheduled one carries its schedule text; EXECUTE TASK runs the body once per call, so three calls insert three rows, and it accepts a SCHEMA-QUALIFIED name. A task body may be any statement, including an aggregating INSERT ... SELECT. EXECUTE TASK on a missing name answers Snowflake's own sentence with the fully-qualified name and no preamble. The execution HISTORY records each run: two successful runs are two SUCCEEDED rows, and a task whose body fails still exists afterwards with one FAILED row, because the scheduler catches the error and records it rather than propagating. And a scheduled task sitting beside a manual one does NOT run when the manual one is executed. Converted 1:1 from scripting/ManualTaskTest (now retired); the Java read the Task object out of the catalog through engine.getCatalog(), which has no SQL surface, so the converted tests read SHOW TASKS for the schedule and state and TABLE(INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TASK_HISTORY()) for the execution history - the success and failure COUNTS the Java asserted are the counts of SUCCEEDED and FAILED rows there. The one claim not carried over is getScheduleType() being non-null, which SHOW TASKS does not expose separately; the schedule text it reports implies it.

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE source_data (id INTEGER, value VARCHAR)
CREATE TABLE summary (total INTEGER, distinct_count INTEGER)
INSERT INTO source_data VALUES (1, 'A'), (2, 'B'), (3, 'A')
CREATE TASK summarize_task WAREHOUSE = 'compute_wh' AS INSERT INTO summary SELECT COUNT(*) as total, COUNT(DISTINCT value) as distinct_count FROM source_data
EXECUTE TASK summarize_task
SELECT total, distinct_count FROM summary
CREATE TABLE task_log (id INTEGER, message VARCHAR)
CREATE TASK my_manual_task WAREHOUSE = 'compute_wh' AS INSERT INTO task_log VALUES (1, 'Execution')
EXECUTE TASK my_manual_task
EXECUTE TASK my_manual_task
